host.name: zbook
host.gpu: AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 40 CU, unified LPDDR5X)
host.note: Every figure is gfx1151. No gfx1100 hardware was available.

changes: The row loop inside the query/key dot product was rolled, because its bound (`r_valid`, how many of the block's eight rows still have query data) is only known at run time. A rolled loop over an array of per-row accumulators and an array of per-row query pointers forces dynamically indexed registers -- v_movreld/v_movrels pairs -- and the body cost 46 instructions per (row, eight dimensions) against eight multiply-adds and two 16-byte loads. Blocks that own a full row set now take a specialized unrolled path; every block but the last one does.

Both key walks in the accumulation loop now carry running pointers and a 32-bit trip count instead of indexing the weights by the key and counting in int64. The rolled form spent a shift, an add, a 64-bit carry chain and a scalar-to-vector move per key on addressing, and could not be unrolled enough to hide shared-memory latency behind the arithmetic. Each walk is unrolled four keys deep.

instruction_counts_per_lane_tile.command: rocprofv3 --pmc SQ_INSTS_VALU SQ_INSTS_SALU SQ_INSTS_LDS SQ_INSTS_FLAT SQ_INSTS_BRANCH (dispatch 1, 229504 lane-tiles per call)
instruction_counts_per_lane_tile.note: Counters are deterministic, so they are the primary evidence. The global-load count falling by 64% is a second-order effect: with the row loop unrolled the compiler schedules the query reads far better than it could around dynamic register indexing.

paired_kernel_ab.command: python3 scripts/yue2_attention_bench.py --repeat 20, alternating the two sources in one session
paired_kernel_ab.note: Absolute times drift up to 15% between batches on this host, so only the paired ratio is claimed.

rows_per_block_recheck.conclusion: Eight rows is still the optimum, but sixteen is now only 27% behind instead of 45%, because the row loop no longer costs 46 instructions per row.

bit_parity.result: bit-identical to the parent kernel (max abs diff 0.0)

unit_tests.coverage_note: The parametrization covers blocks with a full row set (nar_rows 40), a partial one (7, 1, 34), and a head_dim that is not a multiple of eight (100), so all three paths in the kernel are exercised.

remaining_gap.reference_measurement: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace on the pinned upstream running the same case: attn_fwd at grid (2688, 16, 1) with a 128-thread workgroup, 1792 calls at 2.310 ms each, 4.140 s total. That is 12.4 TFLOP/s of attention arithmetic.
remaining_gap.note: This kernel is scalar FP32 FMA; the reference is a tensor-core flash attention. The scalar path's arithmetic ceiling is 25.6 TFLOP/s of which this kernel keeps roughly a quarter as useful math, so the remaining distance is a kernel-design change (matrix cores) rather than more loop surgery.
